findings.problem: Both private lemmas evaluate a diagram map on an element as a relative norm on the underlying invariants. They do it by hand with a three-step `calc`: `restrictedNormDiagram_map` (simp), then `relativeNormHom_apply` (not simp), then `relativeNorm_coe` (simp). Because `relativeNormHom_apply` is not simp, the chain `(restrictedNormDiagram A).map h x` → `relativeNormHom` → `relativeNorm` → `LevelCompact.relativeNorm` stops halfway under `simp`. The same ~20-line proof is therefore written twice, once for `full A` and once for a general `B`. They are the same statement, since `full A` is a `RestrictedLevelCompactRep` whose `rep` is `A.rep`. Neither is public or simp, so downstream files cannot normalise `((restrictedNormDiagram B).map h x).1` either.
findings.proposed_change: Make the normal form of a diagram map on an element simp-reachable. Tag `RestrictedLevelSystem.relativeNormHom_apply` with `@[simp]`; its LHS is a bundled-hom application and its RHS is the plain `relativeNorm`, so there is no cycle with `relativeNorm_coe`. Alternatively, state one public `@[simp]` lemma `restrictedNormDiagram_map_coe` for a general `RestrictedLevelCompactRep` (the content of `normDiagram_map_coe`). Then delete `fullNorm_map_coe` and use the general lemma at `B := full A` (the use sites at lines 81, 88, 159 and 259). The `calc` bodies would reduce to `simp`.
findings.benefit: This gives one canonical rewrite from `((restrictedNormDiagram B).map h x).1` to `LevelCompact.relativeNorm … x.1`, usable by `simp` in every downstream file. It removes a duplicated lemma and the long `congrArg`/`calc` plumbing in `fullNormLimit_projection_mem_iff`, `universalNorm_relativeNorm_surjective` and `fullPoint_coefficient_compatible`.

findings.problem: The comparison isomorphism is a `def` built from a tactic block (`asIso comparison`). `simp` therefore cannot see that `(restrictedNormLimitIso B).hom` is `lim.map (restrictedNormDiagramMap (fullInclusion B))`. The projection equation `hom ≫ π full U = π B U ≫ groupMap (fullInclusion B) U` is the canonical normal form for this iso, but it is not simp. `fullInclusion_limitMap_π` is already an instance of the simp lemma `limit.map_π`, so tagging it would add nothing. The proofs and the example file avoid `simp`: they unfold by hand with `ConcreteCategory.congr_hom`, `change`, and `simpa only [full] using hval`. The `@[simp]` lemma `fullInclusion_apply` is then applied only by explicit `.trans` chains (lines 308–309, 336), not by the simplifier.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `restrictedNormLimitIso_hom_π` as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`, so that `hom ≫ limit.π …` rewrites to `limit.π … ≫ groupMap (fullInclusion B) U`. Optionally add a `@[simp]` lemma `restrictedNormLimitIso_hom : (restrictedNormLimitIso B).hom = lim.map (restrictedNormDiagramMap (fullInclusion B))`. After that, the pointwise goals at lines ~300–336 could be closed by `simp` using `groupMap_apply`, `coefficientMap_coe` and `fullInclusion_apply`. I have not run this, so confluence with `limit.map_π` should be checked once the lemma is added.
findings.benefit: Users of the isomorphism would get its projection behaviour from `simp` and `simp [reassoc]` instead of rebuilding it with `congr_hom`. The `simpa only [full]` unfolding and the manual `.trans` chains in `fullInclusion_limitMap_bijective` become unnecessary.
